newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower on Brazil purchases.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower on Brazil purchases.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended lower on Thursday, in line with losses in soybeans, amid news a U.S. processor bought three cargoes of soybeans, most likely of Brazilian origin, traders said.

An Owensboro Grain Co. official in Owensboro, Ky. confirmed it bought 150,000 tonnes of soybeans and that the beans could come from the U.S., Brazil, Argentina or Paraguay at the seller's option. Trade sources speculated they would be Brazil beans as supplies were cheaper and of better quality.
There were also reports from Brazil that a processor was negotiating to sell soymeal to the U.S.
Brazilian processor Ceval Alimentos said it was in talks to sell an unspecified amount of Brazilian soymeal to a U.S. firm but further details were not available.

A late rally in corn pulled the soy complex off the day's lows. Traders cited rumors a private analytical firm planned to release acreage estimates on Friday and the corn number was expected to be below USDA's initial estimate of 81 million acres released last month at the outlook conference.
Soymeal closed $1.10 per ton lower to $0.20 higher with May unchanged at $266.00. Soyoil closed 0.10 to 0.01 cent per lb lower with May off 0.07 at 25.27 cents.

USDA export sales data offered little hope for the market with soyoil sales virtually non-existent and soymeal below the four-week average. USDA said soyoil exports for the week ended March 6 were at 900 tonnes. Soymeal exports totalled 44,100 tonnes, 47 percent below the four-week average.
On the day, Cargill Inc bought 500 lots July soymeal and 100 lots May, Continental Grain bought 400 Kay and Produce Grain bought 100 May and sold 100 July, traders said.
In soyoil, Produce Grain sold 600 lots May and 100 July, Cargill Inc bought 400 May but sold 300 May and 200 July and ADM sold 200 December.
Prudential Securities bought 800 lots July and Cargill Investor Services and Dean Witter each bought 500 May.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 25,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 33,167 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 24,000 lots, against Wednesday's 31,651 lots.
